newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to pass pension reform act next week - PM.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to pass pension reform act next week - PM.

text.p: Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa on Thursday announced the launch of a long-awaited pension system reform.
"The government will approve a new pension act next week to pave the way for the reform, and send it to the parliament," Matesa told an international investment conference in Zagreb.
"Our current pay-as-you-go system is dead," he said, adding that the government would propose a three-pillar, partly privatised pension system.

The state funds, in which the contributions of working Croats are payed, can barely suffice for pensions and payments of social care to its beneficiaries, including a rising number of jobless and war invalids.

The overhaul of the state-owned pension fund is expected to take several years to complete. It will also require considerable amount of cash which is partly to come from the World Bank in form of a public sector adjustment loan.

Matesa said Croatia needs a better social security network to absorb the future schokc of radical company restructuring which would lead to substantial lay-offs. -- Zagreb Newsroom, Kolumbina Bencevic, 385-1-4557075
